title: CompTIA A+ Core 1 vs Core 2: What's the Difference?
excerpt: You need both to get A+. Core 1 is hardware and networking; Core 2 is software and security.
description: CompTIA A+ Core 1 vs Core 2: what each exam covers, the passing scores, and which one to take first.
body:
To earn CompTIA A+, you need to pass two exams: Core 1 and Core 2. They cover different topics, and you can take them in either order.

## Core 1 (220-1201)

- Mobile devices, networking and hardware
- Virtualisation and cloud computing
- Hardware and network troubleshooting
- Passing score: 675 on a scale of 100 to 900

## Core 2 (220-1202)

- Operating systems
- Security
- Software troubleshooting
- Operational procedures
- Passing score: 700 on a scale of 100 to 900

## Which to take first?

Most people take Core 1 first, because hardware and networking basics make Core 2 easier to understand. If you already work with operating systems and support tickets, starting with Core 2 can work too.

## How to prepare

- Use the official exam objectives as your checklist
- Study one domain at a time
- Book each exam when you score 85% or more consistently in practice
